chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah, from 'Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) in

When a woman says to her husband, 'My slave girl is for you,' he said: 'Her private part is not permissible to him unless she sells it to him or gifts it to him.' The meaning in this report is that we interpret it as: if she says, 'It is for you, excluding the private part,' regarding her service, because it is known from the custom of women that they do not consider their husbands' intercourse with their slave girls to be permissible [by default], and if the matter is as we have said, then his private part is not permissible to her in any case.
ai.seo_question: Does a wife's gift of her slave girl to her husband include the right of sexual intercourse?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi presents this narration from Imam al-Sadiq to clarify the legal nuance of a wife gifting her slave girl to her husband, distinguishing between the transfer of ownership and the specific right of sexual consummation (*istimta'*). The Imam explains that since it is customary for women not to include their husband's sexual access to their personal slaves unless specified, the default ruling is that the husband does not automatically gain the right to intercourse with the gifted slave girl. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of relying on customary practice (*'urf*) to interpret ambiguous transfers of rights within the family structure.
